Isnad is a plain 4-link sequential chain (no plural verb / coordinating wa..wa.., so no coordinate-group topology issue here): Muḥammad b. al-Muthannā (حَدَّثَنَا بِهِ ... قَالَ) > ʿUmar b. ʿAlī (نا عُمَرُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ — vocalized ʿayn-damma/meem-fatha/ra-damma = ʿUmar, not ʿAmr) > Abū Ḥāzim (عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ) > Sahl b. Nothing in the Arabic supports "was a devout worshipper" (fabricated addition) or the intensified "would not even move" (yaltafitu is specifically about turning/looking around, not all bodily movement — an overstatement/inversion of degree). Restored a literal, faithful rendering of the matn and kept the ᴿᴬ convention this file already uses for ؓ on Abu Bakr (see the immediately preceding record, id 28000024). Read the Arabic myself (bazzar.json line 9446, id 28000029) word by word and confirmed both parts of the audit's diagnosis, plus found one additional error the audit missed.

Isnad: "أَخبرَنِي عَبْدُ الْقُدُّوسِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْكَبِيرِ الْعَطَّارُ قَالَ نا أَمْرُو بْنُ عَاصِمٍ الْكِلَابِيُّ قَالَ نا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ ثَابِتٍ عَنْ أَنَسٍ" reads: "ʿAbd al-Quddūs b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Kabir al-ʿAṭṭār informed me, [who] said: ʿAmr b. ʿĀṣim al-Kilābī narrated to us, [who] said: Sulaymān b. al-Mughīra narrated to us, from Thābit, from Anas."

1. Confirmed: the first narrator's name in the Arabic is unambiguously "عَبْدُ الْقُدُّوسِ" (ʿAbd al-Quddūs), not "ʿAbdullāh" — the existing English invented a different name entirely. Fixed.
2. Confirmed: "الْكِلَابِيُّ" (al-Kilābī) is a tribal nisba (Banū Kilāb, a well-attested Basran narrator ʿAmr b. ʿĀṣim al-Kilābī), not an occupational term — "the dog handler" is a fabricated/false rendering. Fixed by transliterating the nisba rather than inventing an occupation, matching how the audit flagged it.

4. New finding beyond the audit's hint: the closing isnad-critique/grading sentence was truncated. The Arabic ends with "وَهَذَا الْحَدِيثُ لَا نَعْلَمُ رَوَاهُ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ إِلَّا عَمْرُو بْنُ عَاصِمٍ وَلَا يُرْوَى عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ إِلَّا مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ وَالْإِسْنَادُ إِسْنَادٌ صَحِيحٌ" ("we do not know this hadith narrated from Sulaymān b. al-Mughīra except by ʿAmr b. ʿĀṣim, nor is it narrated from Abu Bakr except by this route, and the isnad is sahih") but the English collapsed all of that into just "This is a sahih narration," dropping the uniqueness-of-transmission critique entirely. Restored it.
5. Left untouched: the opening comment "قَالَ اِنَّ حَدِيثَهُمَا لَا نَعْلَمُ سُبْطَانًا مِنْهُمَا إِلَّا قَوْلاً فِي الْمَوْتِ" contains a word ("سُبْطَانًا") that doesn't parse as standard Arabic (likely an OCR/source artifact) — the existing English gloss ("we do not know any tradition of these two except for a saying about death") is a reasonable-enough rendering of the surrounding words and I have no confident alternative reading, so I preserved it rather than guessing. Likewise preserved the Umm Ayman matn sentence and the established idiosyncratic transliteration style (Salīman, Al-Muġira, Thabīt) since those are stylistic, not factual, and already faithful.

rationale: Independently read the Arabic (bazzar.json lines 9668-9684, id 28000043). correctedNarrator: Salamah b. Shabib>Abdur-Razzaq>Ma'mar>al-Zuhri>Urwah>Aishah>Abu Bakr, ᴿᴬ
correctedText: The Prophet ﷺ said, 'We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity.' Abu Bakr said, and this statement has been narrated from Abu Bakr through more than one route, so we have also mentioned it from Aishah, from Abu Bakr.
rationale:
Read the Arabic isnad and matn directly (id 28000044, Musnad al-Bazzar 44):

حَدَّثَنَا سَلَمَةُ بْنُ شَبِيبٍ قَالَ نا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ قَالَ أنا مَعْمَرٌ عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ عَنْ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ عَن النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَا نُورَثُ مَا تَرَكْنَا صَدَقَةٌ. قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَهَذَا الْكَلَامُ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ مِن غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ فَذَكَرْنَاهُ عَن عَائِشَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ أَيْضًا

This is the well-known "golden chain" isnad: Salamah b. Shabib (a known transmitter from Abdur-Razzaq) > Abdur-Razzaq (ibn Humam al-San'ani) > Ma'mar (ibn Rashid) > al-Zuhri > Urwah (ibn al-Zubayr) > Aishah > Abu Bakr — a straight sequential chain (every link uses singular qala/'an, no plural qalu or wa...wa joint-narration verb), so no coordinate-group topology fix is needed here.

I confirm both meaning inversions the audit flagged:
1. "لَا نُورَثُ" (nūrathu) is the passive form ("we are not inherited from"), not active "نُوَرِّثُ" (we do not inherit). The existing English ("We do not inherit what we leave behind but charity") reverses subject/object on the specific Fadak-dispute saying, where the point is that prophets leave no inheritable estate — nothing is inherited from them, only charity remains.
2. "مِن غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ" is a standard hadith-critical idiom meaning "via more than one route/chain" (i.e., corroborated), not "without authority." The existing English ("narrated from him without authority") inverts corroboration into doubt.

I also confirmed the narrator field itself was badly garbled: "Salame b. Shabiq" (misspelled Shabib), a stray transliterated "na" fused onto Abdur-Razzaq's name, "maʿmärع" (Ma'mar with a stray Arabic ع character stuck on), and then the rest of the chain (al-Zuhri, Urwah, Aishah, Abu Bakr) was left as raw untranslated Arabic script instead of being transliterated. None of those are invented names — they all map cleanly onto the real Arabic isnad — so I just transliterated the whole chain correctly and dropped the untranslated fragment, matching the dataset's own separator/naming conventions (checked against sibling records 41–45 in the same file, e.g. record 45 uses "…> al-Qasim b. Muhammad> Aishah, ᴿᴬ").

For the text field, I also replaced the literal Arabic salawat "صلّى الله عليه وسلم" that had been left embedded in the English (untranslated) with the ﷺ glyph, which is this dataset's uniform convention (see records 42, 43, 45). The trailing "قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ …" sentence is al-Bazzar's own editorial note about the hadith's routes of transmission (a normal recurring pattern in this Musnad, confirmed by the near-identical construction in record 45's "Abu Bakr said, and this hadith is included…") — it is genuinely part of this citation, not a disconnected fragment belonging to a different hadith, so I kept it in the main text field rather than cutting it off. No content was dropped; only the narrator-chain and the two inverted/mistranslated clauses needed correction — the reference, arabic, grade, and other fields are untouched.

rationale: Independently translated the Arabic isnad and matn myself before trusting the audit hint, and confirmed both flagged defects are real: (1) the narrator field is genuinely truncated after 2 of 6 names — Zanfal Abu Abdullah al-Arafi, Ibn Abi Mulaykah, Aishah, and Abu Bakr are all present in the Arabic ("...قَالَ نا زَنْفَلٌ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَرَفِيُّ ... قَالَ نا ابْنُ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ عَنْ عَائِشَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ") but absent from the English narrator string; (2) the text field is mostly untranslated Arabic plus the phrase "و رأي ايجابي" ("a positive opinion") which does not exist anywhere in the Arabic — a fabricated injection — while the hadith's actual content, the Prophet's dua "اللَّهُمَّ خِرْ لِي وَاخْتَرْ لِي" (Allahumma khir li wakhtar li), is completely missing from the English. I checked chain topology explicitly: every link uses singular qāla/'an (sequential haddathanā chain), not qālū or coordinating wa...wa..., so a linear ">" chain is correct — no coordinate-group rendering is needed here. I also checked whether the closing sentence about Zanfal ("وَزَنْفَلٌ هَذَا قَدْ حَدَّثَ عَنْهُ...") was a disconnected fragment from another citation; it is not — it is Bazzar's own isnad-critique of Zanfal within this same hadith, so it belongs in the text field (isnad-critique sentence), not appended to the narrator chain. The corrected text field restores the matn (with transliteration + translation) and the genuine isnad-critique sentence, and drops the fabricated "positive opinion" phrase. correctedNarrator: Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Ubayd > Ubayd b. Aqil > Abdul Rahman b. Abi Bakr > Ibn Abi Mulaykah > Aishah > Abu Bakr
correctedText: He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "No prophet died except that he was buried where he died." And Abu Bakr said: I found in my book, from Abu Kurayb, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, who said: Abdul Rahman b. Abi Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Aishah, from Abu Bakr, from the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording. Abu Bakr said: And this saying — we do not know of anyone who narrated it from the Prophet ﷺ except Abu Bakr, and it was narrated from Abu Bakr by Ibn Abbas and Aishah.
rationale:
Independently verified against the Arabic word-by-word; the audit's three diagnoses all hold, plus I found one more narrator-fusion error it missed.

(1) qubida/yuqbadu (root ق-ب-ض, idiomatic for death, "God took his soul") was mistranslated as "captured," and the clause order was inverted ("buried except where captured" vs. the Arabic's "died except buried where died"). Fixed to "No prophet died except that he was buried where he died."

(2) Narrator field fused two distinct people into a fake compound "Abdullah b. Abi Bakr b. Al-Malikah" — the Arabic isnad clearly separates عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ (Abdul Rahman b. Abi Bakr) from عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي مُلَيْكَةَ (Ibn Abi Mulaykah) with "'an" between them. Additionally — not flagged by the audit — the narrator field also fused Muhammad b. Abdullah b. Ubayd (the immediate narrator, "haddathana") with his own grandfather's separately-introduced nasab (قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي جَدِّي عُبَيْدُ بْنُ عَقِيلٍ = "my grandfather Ubayd b. Aqil told me") into one fabricated 4-generation name, silently dropping that link from the chain. Rebuilt the full 6-link chain.

(3) The closing critique sentence وَرَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَعَائِشَةُ names the companion Ibn Abbas explicitly as also transmitting from Abu Bakr; the current English dropped his name for a vague "his father was reported to have said this." Restored "narrated from Abu Bakr by Ibn Abbas and Aishah." Per the chain-topology rule, this is a note about a different (unstated) transmission line from Abu Bakr, not part of this hadith's own isnad, so I restored it in the text but correctly did NOT append Ibn Abbas to the narrator chain.

No qālū/plural-verb or wa...wa... joint-narration construction appears anywhere in this record — the chain is fully sequential (qala...qala...'an...'an), so that part of rule 4 doesn't apply here. Also cleaned up the alternate-isnad sentence's mistranslated "بِنَحْوِهِ" (was rendered as "used to say something like this," corrected to "with similar wording") and a stray "I heard" that had turned a chain into a false claim of direct hearing across multiple links. The opening clause "He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say" was already accurate and is preserved unchanged.

correctedNarrator: Salamah b. Shabib and al-Fadl b. Sahl said, Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Madani said, Sulaiman b. Bilal said, 'Abdu l-Hakim b. 'Abdullah b. Abi Farwa said, Ya'qub b. 'Utbah said, 'Urwah said, 'Aisha said:
correctedText: When 'Abdullah b. Abi Bakr died and was wept over, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) came out and said: I apologize to you for the behavior of these women; they are not far removed from the days of pre-Islamic ignorance. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, 'The deceased is scalded with boiling water because of the weeping of the living.' Abu Bakr [al-Bazzar] said: We do not know this hadith to be narrated from Abu Bakr, from the Prophet ﷺ, by any route other than this one. 'Abdu l-Hakim b. 'Abdullah is a man from the people of Medina, well known and sound in hadith, and Ya'qub b. 'Utbah is well known. As for this Muhammad b. al-Hasan, he is weak (layyin) in hadith because he narrated hadiths in which he was not corroborated, though a group of the people of knowledge did narrate from him. He is known as Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Zubalah al-Makhzumi.
rationale:
Verified against the Arabic directly (bazzar.json lines 9785-9801, id 28000050). The audit's core diagnosis holds on both counts:

1. MATN INVERSION/FLATTENING (confirmed): The Arabic says إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ الْمَيِّتُ يُنْضَحُ عَلَيْهِ الْحَمِيمُ بِبُكَاءِ الْحَيِّ = "I heard the Messenger of Allah say: the deceased is scalded with boiling water (al-hamim) because of the weeping of the living." The existing English ("I heard from the Prophet that the dead is mourned by the living") deletes al-hamim (boiling water) and the punishment verb yundah ('is scalded/splashed upon'), turning a torment-warning hadith into a bland statement about mourning. Restored. Also restored a dropped clause: بُكِيَ عَلَيْهِ ("he [the deceased] was wept over") — the event that provoked Abu Bakr's speech — which had vanished entirely from the old translation (it jumped straight to "when he died, Abu Bakr got up and said..."). Also fixed a mistranslated idiom: حَدِيثُ عَهْدٍ بِجَاهِلِيَّةٍ ("not far removed from the days of jahiliyyah," an idiom for "recently come from") had been rendered as the nonsensical "a tradition in the era of ignorance."

2. NARRATOR-IDENTITY CONFLATION (confirmed): The closing isnad-critique sentence وَهُوَ يُعْرَفُ بِمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ زُبَالَةَ الْمَخْزُومِيِّ ("and he is known as Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Zubalah al-Makhzumi") grammatically refers back to Muhammad b. al-Hasan (the subject of the preceding weak/layyin al-hadith assessment), not to 'Abdu l-Hakim b. 'Abdullah. The old English wrongly attached this alias to 'Abdu l-Hakim. I also restored the entire isnad-critique passage that had been dropped wholesale: the "we know this only via this one route" note, and the individual gradings of 'Abdu l-Hakim (reliable/well-known), Ya'qub b. 'Utbah (well-known), and Muhammad b. al-Hasan (weak/layyin, uncorroborated narrations, though transmitted from by scholars) — none of which survived into the old "text" field at all.

Additional fix beyond the audit's hint: the narrator chain named "Salma b. Shabi'" — Arabic سَلَمَةُ بْنُ شَبِيبٍ is "Salamah b. Shabib" (a known Bazzar informant), not "Salma" (a different, typically feminine name) — an invented/misread name per correction criterion #1.

Chain topology was already correct and left untouched: قَالَا (dual "they both said") for Salamah b. Shabib and al-Fadl b. Sahl was already rendered as a coordinate "X and Y said," not a false sequential chain, so no topology fix was needed there. No disconnected trailing fragment exists in this record (unlike some others) — the whole passage belongs to this one hadith's isnad/matn/critique, so the corrected chain runs the full length of the Arabic isnad ending at 'Aisha.

Net scope: full retranslation of "text" (matn + critique were both substantively wrong/truncated), narrow fix to "narrator" (one misread name, plus moving the matn-introductory clause out of the narrator field into text where the actual reported speech begins).

correctedNarrator: Abu Kurayb > Ishaq b. Mansoor > Ja'far al-Ahmar > al-Sariyy b. Isma'il > Qays, b. Abi Hazim
correctedText: He said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found that he had already passed away, so I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Disowning one's lineage, even if it is a small matter, is disbelief (kufr) against Allah." We do not know this saying to be narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through Abu Bakr, from him, and it was narrated from Abu Bakr by Qays b. Abi Hazim with this chain of narration. Abu Ma'mar also narrated it from Abu Bakr, but they differed concerning the raising of Abu Ma'mar's report to the Prophet: a group narrated it from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah b. Murrah, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abu Bakr, as a stopped report (mawquf), while some of them narrated it as raised to the Prophet (musnad). But whoever raised it is not an authority in hadith. And al-Sariyy b. Isma'il is not strong; al-Zuhri and many others narrated from him, and they tolerated his hadith.
rationale:
I verified the audit's diagnosis directly against the Arabic (Musnad al-Bazzar 53) and confirmed all three problems, plus one more the hint didn't mention:

1. Fabricated narrator "Abu Sa'id Khudri": the Arabic isnad is حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ ... عَنِ السَّرِيُّ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ قَيْسِ بْنِ أَبِي حَازِمٍ قَالَ قَدِمْتُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ... — the matn is introduced by a plain قَالَ ("he said") whose subject is the last-named narrator, Qays b. Abi Hazim. "Abu Sa'id Khudri" appears nowhere in the Arabic; it's a pure AI invention. Fixed by starting the text with "He said:" (referring back to Qays, already correctly the last link in the narrator field).

2. السَّرِيُّ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ (al-Sariyy b. Isma'il) was mistranslated as a different person, "Nafi', b. Ismail," in the narrator chain — corrected. (I also fixed "Abu Kurrah" -> "Abu Kurayb" for أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ, a genuine well-known kunya misspelled in the same field; this wasn't in the hint but is a real name error of the same kind.)

3. The commentary conflated الْأَعْمَشِ (al-A'mash) and عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُرَّةَ ('Abdullah b. Murrah) — two separate, sequential links (فَرَوَاهُ جَمَاعَةٌ عَنِ الْأَعْمَشِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مُرَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي مَعْمَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ مَوْقُوفًا) — into one garbled name "al-Amashi b. Murrah," and the rest of that sentence plus everything after it degenerated into untranslated/garbled mixed Arabic-English. This is a genuine sequential 'an-chain (not a joint/plural narration), so I rendered it as a normal chain: "from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah b. Murrah, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abu Bakr" — not a coordinate group.

4. Beyond the hint: (a) قُبِضَ ("he had passed away/died") was mistranslated as "when he was buried" — a real meaning shift (Qays arrived to find the Prophet already deceased, not specifically at/after burial); fixed to "passed away," matching this same book's own established rendering of qubida elsewhere (e.g. id 28000... "When the Prophet ﷺ passed away..."). (b) The clause وَإِنْ دَقَّ ("even if it is a small/slight matter") qualifying the disowning-of-lineage statement was dropped entirely from the current English; restored. (c) The whole final isnad-critique/grading sentences — "the one who raised it [as musnad] is not an authority in hadith," "al-Sariyy b. Isma'il is not strong [i.e. weak]," "al-Zuhri and many others narrated from him, and they tolerated his hadith" — were left as incoherent transliteration-like gibberish in the current English (e.g. "لاهو رأي سلبي في الحديث والسر بنسماءهو رأي ضعيف"); these are restored as genuine, connected hadith-grading content (not a disconnected/different-citation fragment — it's Bazzar's own continuous critique of this same hadith's alternate transmission), so I kept it in the "text" field rather than truncating it out of the narrator chain.

The narrator field's primary isnad (Abu Kurayb > Ishaq b. Mansoor > Ja'far al-Ahmar > al-Sariyy b. Isma'il > Qays b. Abi Hazim) is a clean, fully-connected sequential chain with no coordinate/joint narration and no disconnected trailing fragment, so nothing needed to be cut from it — only the one wrong name (plus the incidental Kurayb/Kurrah spelling) needed fixing. Everything else already accurate (Ishaq b. Mansoor, Ja'far al-Ahmar, Qays b. Abi Hazim, and most of the critique's factual content) was preserved as-is; I did not restyle parts that were already correct.

correctedNarrator: Muhammad b. al-Muthannā>Abdullāh b. Dāwud>Ibn Akhi Muhammad b. al-Munkadir>Muhammad b. al-Munkadir>Jābir
correctedText: Umar said, 'O Abu Bakr, you are the best of people!' Then he replied, 'Since you have said that, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that no one ever excelled Umar in virtue since the sun rose.' This hadith was narrated only by this route. And no one is known to have narrated from Ibn Akhi Muhammad b. al-Munkadir except Abdullāh b. Dāwud al-Wāsiṭī, and he did not accept it but on what is in his chain of narration because there is merit for Umar.
rationale:
Read the Arabic isnad directly: "حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى قَالَ نا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ دَاوُدَ قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمُثَنَّى وَكَانَ صَاحِبَ سُنَّةٍ قَالَ نا ابْنُ أَخِي مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ عَنْ عَمِّهِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ عَنْ جَابِرٍ". This is a plain sequential chain (each link uses "qāla"/"ʿan", no "qālū" plural or coordinating wa...wa... requiring a coordinate-group rendering): Muhammad b. al-Muthannā (the compiler's direct teacher) > Abdullāh b. Dāwud > "Ibn Akhi Muhammad b. al-Munkadir" (an unnamed narrator identified only as "the nephew of Muhammad b. al-Munkadir") > his uncle Muhammad b. al-Munkadir > Jābir (the Companion source).

The audit's diagnosis of the narrator field checks out: the existing value "Muhammad b. al-Munkadir>Abdullāh b. Dāwud>Muhammad b. al-Munkadir>,هو رأي ايجابي" (a) wrongly opens with "Muhammad b. al-Munkadir" instead of the actual first link Muhammad b. al-Muthannā (a similar-sounding but distinct name), (b) drops the "Ibn Akhi..." nephew link entirely, (c) omits Jābir, the Companion source, and (d) appends "هو رأي ايجابي" ("it is a positive opinion") — I confirmed this Arabic string does not appear anywhere in the record's actual "arabic" field; it is a pure fabrication, not a misplaced fragment of a real citation, so it is simply dropped rather than treated as a topology issue.

Independently verifying the "text" field (which the audit said to leave untouched), I found a real reversed-direction error the audit missed: the Arabic isnad-critique sentence "وَابْنُ أَخِي مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْمُنْكَدِرِ لَا نَعْلَمُ حَدَّثَ عَنْهُ إِلَّا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ دَاوُدَ الْوَاسِطِيُّ" means "no one is known to have narrated FROM [the nephew] except Abdullāh b. Dāwud" (i.e., Abdullāh b. Dāwud is the one reporting from the obscure nephew, matching the isnad given earlier in the same hadith). The existing English inverted this to "Ibn Akhi Muhammad b. al-Munkadir has not been reported to have narrated anything except from Abdullāh b. Dāwud" — i.e., it makes the nephew the receiver from Abdullāh b. Dāwud, backwards from the actual transmission direction. I fixed this reversal and corrected "the Wāsidī" to "al-Wāsiṭī" (a transliteration typo for الْوَاسِطِيُّ). I also restored a small dropped clause, "أَمَا إِذْ قُلْتَ ذَاكَ" ("Since you have said that"), which was left untranslated in Abu Bakr's reply. Everything else in the text — the Umar/Abu Bakr mutual-praise exchange itself, the "narrated only by this route" grading note, and the closing "merit for Umar" sentence — is faithful and was left untouched, consistent with the rule to preserve accurate parts rather than rewrite for style.

correctedNarrator: ʿAbdu r-rahmān b. al-ghasyil>Shuraḥbīl b. Saʿd>Jābir>Abū Bakr
correctedText: The Prophet said: Beware of the Fire, even if with half a date. And this hadith was narrated only by a man in Basra, from Zayd b. al-Hubab, and he was accused of fabrication regarding it. It is said that it has no basis via this route. So we kept away from mentioning him.
rationale:
Read the Arabic myself: "وَرَوَى عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْغَسِيلِ عَنْ شُرَحْبِيلَ بْنِ سَعْدٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالَ اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ وَهَذَا الْحَدِيثُ إِنَّمَا حَدَّثَ بِهِ رَجُلٌ كَانَ بِالْبَصْرَةِ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ الْحُبَابِ وَكَانَ مُتَّهَمًا فِيهِ يُقَالُ أَنَّ لَيْسَ لَهُ أَصْلٌ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ فَأَمْسَكْنَا عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ".

Narrator/isnad field: already accurate. It's a plain sequential chain (Abd al-Rahman b. al-Ghasil > Shurahbil b. Sa'd > Jabir > Abu Bakr, all connected with singular "'an... 'an..."), no plural "qālū"/coordinating "wa" requiring a coordinate-group rendering, no invented names, no disconnected trailing fragment, and it matches this file's convention of not appending "the Prophet" to the narrator chain (checked other records — none do). So correctedNarrator is unchanged.

Text/critical-apparatus sentence: confirmed the audit's core findings against the Arabic myself —
1. "بِالْبَصْرَةِ" (in Basra, the city) was mistranslated as "sighted" (confusing al-Basrah with baṣar/sight). Fixed to "in Basra."
2. "عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ الْحُبَابِ" (from Zayd b. al-Hubab) — the named source the anonymous Basran cited — was dropped entirely from the English. Restored it. (Note: contra the audit's phrasing, Zayd b. al-Hubab himself is not "the suspect" — grammatically "كَانَ مُتَّهَمًا فِيهِ" and "فَأَمْسَكْنَا عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ" [so we withheld from *naming* him] both refer back to the unnamed "رَجُلٌ كَانَ بِالْبَصْرَةِ", since he's the one never given a name in the text — Zayd is already named, so there'd be nothing to "withhold." I phrased the correction to keep this ambiguity/attribution as the Arabic has it, rather than asserting Zayd was the accused one.)
3. "وَكَانَ مُتَّهَمًا فِيهِ ... لَيْسَ لَهُ أَصْلٌ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ" (he was accused/suspect regarding it; it has no basis via this route) had been replaced with an invented, unrelated-sounding clause ("He had been mentioned in another narration which states that he doesn't belong to this side at all") that both softens the fabrication accusation and fabricates content not in the Arabic. Restored the actual meaning.
4. Independently (beyond what the audit flagged), I found the matn itself does have a real error the audit called "fine": "وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ" ("even with [only] half a date") was rendered as "even if it were to be a date pit" — a factual mistranslation of "shiqq" (half/piece) as if it were "nawāh" (pit). This is the famous "half a date in charity" hadith (cf. Sahih al-Bukhari), never rendered as "date pit" in any standard translation, so I corrected it too since I was told to trust my own reading over the hint where they conflict.
"So we kept away from mentioning him" was already an accurate rendering of "فَأَمْسَكْنَا عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ" and is preserved unchanged.

correctedNarrator: al-Faḍlu b. Sahl>na Khalaf b. Tamīm>na Mūsā b. Matir al-Qurashī>‘an Abihi>‘an Abī Hurayrah that Abū Bakr ؓ
correctedText: He said to his son, 'O my son, if something happens among the people, then go to the cave in which you saw me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hide, and stay there, for your provision will come to you there, morning and evening.' We do not know this hadith to have been narrated by anyone other than Khalaf b. Tamīm.
rationale: Independently translated the Arabic (id 28000072 / idInBook 72, bazzar.json line 10143-10157) and confirmed the audit's diagnosis. Narrator fix: the Arabic chain (حَدَّثَنَا الْفَضْلُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ قَالَ نا خَلَفُ بْنُ تَمِيمٍ قَالَ نا مُوسَى بْنُ مَطِيرٍ الْقُرَشِيُّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرٍ ؓ) is a plain sequential isnad with no plural verbs/coordination, so no coordinate-group topology fix is needed. However the old narrator field truncated the chain right before "Abū Bakr" (dropping the actual Companion-source of the report) and wrongly attached the ؓ symbol to Abū Hurayrah instead of Abū Bakr, plus was missing a ">" separator. Fixed by extending the chain to end "...‘an Abī Hurayrah that Abū Bakr ؓ", matching this same book's established convention for such chains (compare id 28000090: "...from Anas that Abu Bakr narrated to him"). Text fix: the matn قَالَ لِابْنِهِ يَا بَنِي إِنْ حَدَثَ فِي النَّاسِ فَأْتِ الْغَارَ الَّذِي رَأَيْتَنِي اخْتَبَأْتُ فِيهِ أَنَا وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فَكُنْ فِيهِ فَإِنَّهُ سَيَأْتِيكَ فِيهِ رِزْقُكَ غُدَوَةً وَعَشِيَّةً is Abu Bakr COMMANDING his son (two imperatives: فَأْتِ "go" to the cave, فَكُنْ "stay" in it) if trouble occurs among the people, since his provision will reach him there. The old English dropped both commands, invented a vague/unsourced "and that is where he will find you" with no antecedent in the Arabic, dropped "يَا بَنِي" (O my son), and reversed the meaning of إِنْ حَدَثَ فِي النَّاسِ ("if something happens among the people") into "if you hear about people in the future." The closing critique sentence (لَا نَعْلَمُ رَوَاهُ إِلَّا خَلَفُ بْنُ تَمِيمٍ, "we do not know it narrated except by Khalaf b. Tamim") was already present and substantively accurate in the old English, so its meaning/wording was preserved essentially unchanged in the corrected text.

correctedNarrator: Ahmad b. Aban al-Qurashi > Anas b. 'Iyad > Yunus b. Yazid > Al-Hakam b. ʿAbdullāh > Qasim b. Muhammad > Aisha
correctedText: She said, 'My father said to me, "Shall I not teach you a supplication that the Messenger of Allah taught me, which 'Isa (Jesus) used to teach the disciples: If you had a debt like Mount Uhud and you said it, Allah would settle it for you?"' She said, 'I said, "Yes."' He said, 'Say: O Allah, Reliever of grief and Remover of hardship, Answerer of the call of the distressed, Most Merciful of this world and the next, You are my Most Merciful, so have mercy on me with a mercy that makes me independent of anyone besides You.' This hadith - we do not know of anyone who narrated it from the Messenger of Allah except Abu Bakr ؓ, nor do we know of any route for it other than this one. And we do not know of anyone who narrated this hadith from Yunus b. Yazid except Anas b. 'Iyad, Sulayman b. Bilal, and 'Abdullah b. 'Umar. Al-Hakam b. 'Abdullah is weak (da'if). We have only mentioned this hadith because we do not know it from the Messenger of Allah except by this route, and so we have written it down.
rationale:
Read the Arabic word-by-word myself (record at bazzar.json lines 10239-10255, id 28000078). The audit's core diagnosis holds up:

1. Narrator name error: "أَنَسُ بْنُ عِيَاضٍ" (Anas b. 'Iyad, the well-known narrator Abu Damrah) was garbled in English as "Anas b. Abiya'a" — an invented, unidentifiable name. Fixed to "Anas b. 'Iyad." The rest of the chain (Ahmad b. Aban al-Qurashi > ... > Yunus b. Yazid > Al-Hakam b. ʿAbdullāh > Qasim b. Muhammad > Aisha) is a straightforward sequential isnad in the Arabic (no plural "qālū"/coordinating "wa...wa..." verb governing the chain itself), so no coordinate-group restructuring was needed there — I left those names untouched since they already map correctly to the Arabic.

2. Exchange-direction garble confirmed: Arabic is "قَالَتْ قَالَ لِي أَبِي" = "She [Aisha] said: My father said to me...". The English had turned "أبي" (my father) into a vocative "Abu," making it read as Aisha addressing someone named "Abu" and asking to be taught — reversing who is teaching whom. Fixed so her father is the one initiating and teaching her.

3. Matn restoration confirmed as the audit described: the Arabic dua "اللَّهُمَّ فَارِجَ الْهَمِّ وَكَاشِفَ الْكَرْبِ مُجِيبَ دَعْوَةِ الْمُضْطَرِّ رَحْمَانَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ أَنْتَ رَحْمَانِي فَارْحَمْنِي رَحْمَةً تُغْنِينِي بِهَا عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ" (O Allah, Reliever of grief, Remover of hardship, Answerer of the call of the distressed...) was entirely dropped and replaced with the fabricated, unrelated "say, 'I will pay my debt.'" Restored the actual dua. Also fixed "قُلْتِيهِ ... لَقَضَاهُ اللَّهُ عَنْكِ" (if you said it, Allah would settle/pay off the debt for you) which had been mistranslated as "Allah would forgive you."

4. The entire closing isnad-critique/grading sentence — "هذا الحديث لا نعلم أحدًا رواه عن رسول الله إلا أبو بكر ؓ ... والحكم بن عبد الله ضعيف ... فلذلك كتبناه" (this hadith is known only via Abu Bakr, only via this one route; only Anas b. 'Iyad, Sulayman b. Bilal, and 'Abdullah b. 'Umar are known to narrate it from Yunus b. Yazid; al-Hakam b. 'Abdullah is weak; we recorded it only because we know it by no other route) — was completely missing; the English text cut off mid-sentence after "And he said,". This is restored in full. This grading sentence's own list of alternate transmitters ("except Anas b. 'Iyad, Sulayman b. Bilal, and 'Abdullah b.
